studies.source: BOJ staff working paper (Sasaki, Yamamoto, Nakajima 2023) nonlinear pass-through — as cited by Daiwa, Apr 2026 (secondary citation)
studies.note: ~0.024pt per 1% yen move above the threshold (2000-2023 sample), ~0.0365pt per 1% (Daiwa's 2000-2025 update); below the threshold effect is near zero. x10 for a 10% move already beyond the threshold.

studies.source: Daiwa Securities, Mar 2026 (equilibrium price model, 50% firm pass-through)
studies.note: Crude +50% lifts CPI ~0.6pt; pro-rated linearly to +10% (~0.12pt). Not a BOJ number.

qualitative: BOJ does not publish a per-10% crude-oil rule of thumb for CPI. Apr 2026 Outlook Box 2 gives the transmission: a +100% crude shock lifts petrochemical basic products ~47% within a month, synthetic resins ~18% in 3-5 months, plastics/rubber ~6% within 6 months, and final goods/services (autos +3.8%, accommodation/eating out +3.1%) within ~12 months; first-round pass-through is ~50% (all industries) / ~25% (manufacturing) smaller than in the 1970s oil crises.

BOJ Jul 2026 Outlook: oil pass-through is running faster than in 2022 in business-to-business prices and is expected to spread to a wide range of consumer prices; a Jul Box also finds a global-demand shock lifts CPI ex food & energy persistently (+0.6% after 12 quarters per 1 s.d.).
No official BOJ wage-to-CPI sensitivity was located for this compilation (flagged as a gap).

korea.label: Korea

studies.source: Bank of Korea, 'Price stability target operation review, H1 2026' (17 Jun 2026) — via Seoul Economic Daily
studies.horizon: passes into industrial goods & services with ~6m lag; lasts ~1yr
studies.note: Oil +10% raises core inflation by up to 0.1pt; indirect effects explain ~20% of CPI inflation in an oil-decline phase.

studies.source: KDI, 'Impact of recent international oil price increase on consumer prices' (May 2026) — Dubai crude +10%
studies.note: CPI +0.11pt for an ordinary oil rise vs +0.20pt when the rise comes from shipping/transport uncertainty (Hormuz). Petroleum products +2.0pt vs +2.7pt. Core ~0 vs +0.10pt.
Ordinary oil rises barely move core; transport-uncertainty-driven rises add ~0.10pt.

Oil shock from transport disruption could add 1.0-1.6pt to 2026 CPI; 2026 baseline contribution +1.2pt, 2027 +0.9pt; prolonged-high-oil case +1.6 / +1.8pt. Fuel-tax cuts and the price ceiling took roughly 1pt off by Apr-May (BOK/KDI).

studies.source: Hyundai Research Institute (10 May 2026) — via Edaily
studies.note: 10% won depreciation lifts CPI ~0.3pt within 3 months and ~0.5pt at 6 months via import prices (+8-9% at once); larger in a combined oil+FX shock. Private think-tank, not BOK.

qualitative: BOK Working Paper 2023-11 (Kim & Kwark): global shocks hit PPI/import prices more than CPI/core; energy tracks the global factor, the exchange rate tracks the country factor. BOK Monthly Bulletin 2022-4: global-factor commodity inflation raises inflation expectations more than block-specific rises.

BOK did not publish a won-to-CPI rule of thumb in the sources reviewed; BOK's Dec-2025 inflation report said a sustained ~1,470 KRW/USD could keep 2026 headline inflation in the early-to-mid 2% range (qualitative).

ours.note: Local projections 2008-latest (see Korea site, Inflation tab). 90% band wide; sample pre-dates fuel-tax cuts/price cap.
Brent and the won are correlated; estimated jointly.
